goal.content:
An AI agent follows a dialectical protocol: it plans a resolution (a "leap") for a
detected contradiction, executes it via a tool call, and checks the tool's result against its
expectation. When the tool's result contradicts the expectation, the agent is allowed to revise
its plan and try again with a genuinely different resolution.

Observed failure: after a first revision (a new leap, a new tool call, re-checked), the tool's
result contradicted the expectation AGAIN. At this point the agent was supposed to revise a
SECOND time -- propose yet another new leap -- before trying to execute again. Instead, it
skipped proposing a new leap and directly resubmitted the exact same execution plan it had
already tried and that had already failed. This was correctly rejected every time with "revision
must change the plan, not repeat the old one" -- but the agent kept resubmitting the identical
plan anyway, over and over, until it ran out of allowed attempts and the whole run failed.

Diagnose why the agent falls into this specific repeat pattern on the SECOND (and later) revision
specifically, even though it successfully revised correctly the FIRST time, and propose a concrete
fix.
